faqs.q: What is the best pet insurance in 2026?
faqs.a: There is no single best pet insurance - the honest answer depends on which published fact you care about. Lemonade publishes the lowest starting price (from $10/month), Spot publishes the fastest claim payment (48 hours or less, based on Spot admin data 2019-2024) and Fetch publishes the most detailed pricing (breed-by-breed averages with a stated methodology). Compare quotes for your own pet on each official site, because advertised prices are quoted under different deductible, limit and reimbursement conditions.

faqs.q: Which pet insurance is cheapest?
faqs.a: The lowest published starting prices are Lemonade at $10/month for dogs and cats, Spot at $15/month for dogs and $9/month for cats, and Fetch, which does not publish an entry price but publishes averages of $35/month for dogs and $22/month for cats. These figures are not directly comparable: Spot's price assumes an 80% reimbursement rate, a $500 deductible and a $2,500 annual limit for a specific dog in ZIP 32009, while Fetch's average assumes a $10,000 annual limit, a $300 deductible and 80% reimbursement. Your real price comes from a quote on the brand's official site.

faqs.q: Is there a real pet insurance promo code?
faqs.a: Not from these three brands. Their official sitemaps were checked on 2026-09-25 and none contains a promo code or coupon page. The discounts that do exist on the official sites are Lemonade's multi-pet, bundle and annual-payment discounts, Spot's 10% multi-pet discount and its group/employee discount, and Fetch's 10% military discount plus Fetch Deals member savings. Third-party coupon sites are not a source we use.

faqs.q: How long are pet insurance waiting periods?
faqs.a: Published waiting periods: Lemonade 14 days for illnesses and 30 days for orthopedic conditions (preventative package benefits start the day after purchase); Spot typically 14 days, with state-specific variations detailed in its sample policy; Fetch up to 15 days for accident and illness coverage. Coverage for anything that shows signs before those periods end counts as pre-existing.

faqs.q: Does pet insurance cover pre-existing conditions?
faqs.a: No. All three brands state that pre-existing conditions are not covered. Spot additionally publishes that a curable condition which has been symptom-free and treatment-free for 180 days is no longer considered pre-existing and can become eligible. Fetch counts anything that occurred or showed clinical signs before enrolment, during the waiting period, or before the pet's first exam as pre-existing.

faqs.q: Do I need a vet exam to buy pet insurance?
faqs.a: Spot states no vet exam is needed for enrolment and has no upper age limit, with puppies and kittens 8 weeks and older eligible. Fetch covers dogs and cats 6 weeks and older and advises enrolling early so conditions are not later classed as pre-existing. For Lemonade, an enrolment exam requirement is not published on the official pages checked on 2026-09-25.

blocks.h2: How this comparison is built
blocks.html:
There is no lab test for "best pet insurance". What we can do honestly is put the figures each insurer publishes on its own website side by side, keep the condition attached to every figure, and link to the page it came from. Nothing on this page is estimated, scored or taken from a third-party comparison site.

All figures were read from the brands' own pages on 2026-09-25 and are repeated with their conditions in the fact table below. Where an official page does not publish a figure, the cell says not published on the official site instead of a guess.

The three brands quote their prices under different conditions - different deductibles, annual limits and reimbursement rates - so a raw price-to-price comparison would be misleading. That is why this page does not crown a single winner.

blocks.h2: Side-by-side comparison - official published figures only
What each plan is best for, on the published facts
blocks.html:
Lemonade, if you want the lowest published starting price. Its official cost guide lists policies for dogs and cats starting at $10/month, publishes on-average figures of about $48/month for dogs and about $27/month for cats, five deductible options ($100-$1,000) and three official discounts: multi-pet, bundling with other Lemonade policies, and paying annually instead of monthly. A quote is advertised as completable in as little as 90 seconds, and cancelling within the first 30 days gets you a refund. Source: lemonade.com cost guide and lemonade.com/pet-insurance, checked 2026-09-25.

Spot, if published claim speed and a money-back window matter most. Spot states claims are reimbursed in 48 hours or less, with most processed in under 2 business days (its own admin data, 2019-2024), reimburses up to 90% of covered vet bills, offers a 30-day money-back guarantee (not available in NY; 15 days in ME, LA and WA), has no upper age limit and no vet exam to enrol, and gives 10% off every pet enrolled after the first. Source: spotpet.com, spotpet.com/sample-policy and spotpet.com/cat-insurance, checked 2026-09-25.

Fetch, if you want the most transparent pricing and bundled extras. Fetch publishes breed-level averages on its price page - $35/month for dogs and $22/month for cats on average, French Bulldog $71/month, Golden Retriever $50/month, Domestic Shorthair $24/month - with the methodology stated (a $10,000 annual limit, $300 deductible and 80% reimbursement, 07.01.2024-06.30.2025). It also covers sick-visit exam fees up to $250, includes 24/7 online vet visits up to $1,000/year at no extra cost, states waiting periods of up to 15 days and says claims are typically processed in less than 10 days. Veterans and active military get 10% off every month for life. Source: fetchpet.com price page and fetchpet.com, checked 2026-09-25.

blocks.h2: How to choose without a fake ranking
blocks.html:
Run the same exercise the brands run themselves: request a quote for your pet on each official site, then compare the quotes you receive against each other, not against the advertised figures on this page. Advertised figures carry conditions - Spot's "from $15/month" assumes an 80% reimbursement rate, a $500 deductible, a $2,500 annual limit and a specific 2-year-old dog in ZIP 32009 - and your pet will not match those conditions exactly.

Three checks that change the outcome more than the brand name: (1) the waiting period before coverage starts - 14 days, 14 days or up to 15 days here; (2) whether a condition your pet already has counts as pre-existing - none of the three covers pre-existing conditions, though Spot publishes a 180-day symptom- and treatment-free rule for curable conditions; (3) the reimbursement percentage and deductible you choose, which move the premium more than the headline price.

faqs.q: How much does pet insurance cost per month?
faqs.a: The entry points the brands publish are $10/month for dogs and cats at Lemonade, $15/month for dogs and $9/month for cats at Spot, and averages of $35/month for dogs and $22/month for cats at Fetch. faqs.q: What makes one pet insurance quote more expensive than another?

Spot adds that premiums are based on the current age of your pet and may increase at renewal, and that species or breed and home address can change the initial premium.

faqs.q: How can I lower my monthly premium?
faqs.a: Lemonade's cost guide suggests choosing a higher deductible ($100, $250, $500, $750 or $1,000), selecting a lower annual coverage limit, or skipping optional add-ons, and notes that adjusting these levels might lower the premium by 10% or 15% - at the price of being covered for less. Fetch publishes the same mechanic: a higher deductible makes the price lower, and a lower reimbursement rate makes the price lower.

faqs.q: Does location change what pet insurance costs?

The comparison stops there, because Spot's figures assume an 80% reimbursement rate, a $500 or $750 deductible and a $2,500 annual limit for specific pets in specific ZIP codes, while Lemonade's figures assume basic accident and illness coverage. Both brands publish averages only in part: Lemonade publishes about $48/month for dogs and about $27/month for cats, and Spot publishes no average of its own.

faqs.q: What discounts can lower the price?

None of the three brands publishes a promo code page in its official sitemap.

faqs.q: Does pet insurance cost more as my pet gets older?
faqs.a: Spot states on its homepage that premiums are based on the current age of your pet and may increase due to the age of your pet at renewal, and that initial premiums can be affected by species or breed and by home address. Lemonade lists age among the factors that change the cost. The published starting prices on this page therefore describe young pets on the stated configurations, not every age.

Pet insurance prices are quoted, not published as a single number, so this page does two honest things: it repeats the figures each insurer puts on its own website, and it repeats the conditions those figures were calculated under - deductible, annual limit and reimbursement rate - right next to them. Nothing here is estimated, averaged across third-party comparison sites or taken from a broker ranking.

All figures were read from the brands' own pages on 2026-09-25. Where an official page does not publish a figure, the cell says not published on the official site instead of a guess.

The reason the same pet can cost $29 or $336 a month is not only the brand: it is the deductible, limit and reimbursement set chosen, the pet's breed and age, and the state. That is why every row below carries its condition.

blocks.h2: Published prices side by side - with the conditions attached
The same-pet price check Lemonade publishes
blocks.html:
Lemonade's cost guide does something unusual: it prices one identical pet at six companies. For a 4-year-old Goldendoodle in Chicago on 80% co-insurance, the maximum annual limit and a $250 annual deductible it lists Trupanion $336, Healthy Paws $85, Fetch $99, Pets Best $77, ManyPets $73 and Lemonade $61 per month. For a 1-year-old short-haired cat in Danbury, Connecticut on a $250 deductible, 80% co-insurance, the maximum annual limit and no add-ons or discounts it lists Trupanion $58, ManyPets $44, Fetch $36, Pets Best $35 and Lemonade $29. Source: lemonade.com cost guide, checked 2026-09-25.

Treat that spread as a reminder, not a ranking: Lemonade ran the test and published it on its own page, the profiles suit its own pricing, and the page notes the companies could not be made perfectly identical (Trupanion only offered a 90% co-insurance option). The same page also publishes state averages, from $30 to $34 a month in Texas, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Georgia and Michigan up to $45 to $49 in California and Connecticut, using Lemonade's own policy rates as of October 2024.

blocks.h2: What actually moves the number
blocks.html:
Deductible. Lemonade offers $100, $250, $500, $750 or $1,000 and states plainly that a higher deductible lowers your monthly premium. Fetch says the same, and its published average assumes $300. Spot's advertised quotes assume $500 for dogs and $750 for cats. Source: lemonade.com cost guide and fetchpet.com price page, checked 2026-09-25.

Annual limit. Lemonade lets you choose anywhere from $5,000 to $100,000; Spot's advertised quotes use $2,500; Fetch's average uses $10,000. A lower limit buys a lower premium and a smaller maximum payout.

Reimbursement rate. The examples above use 80%; Spot advertises up to 90%; Fetch advertises up to 90%. Lemonade says adjusting these levels might lower your premium by 10% or 15%, and warns that it also means being covered for less when a large bill arrives.

Age, breed and state. Both Lemonade and Spot list age, breed and location as price factors, and Spot states premiums are based on your pet's current age and may increase at renewal. Entry prices on this page are therefore not quotes for an older pet.

blocks.h2: How to get a real number in three steps
blocks.html:
1. Run the same configuration at each brand: pick one deductible (say $500), one annual limit and one reimbursement rate, then take a quote for your own pet at lemonade.com, spotpet.com and fetchpet.com. Lemonade advertises a quote in as little as 90 seconds; Spot's quote entry point is its 'Click For Price' button; Fetch states its quote includes all monthly taxes and fees.

2. Compare those three quotes with each other, not with the advertised figures on this page - advertised figures carry conditions that your pet will not match exactly.

3. Check what the money buys before you pay: waiting periods (14 days illness at Lemonade and in Spot's sample policy, up to 15 days at Fetch), the deductible you chose, and whether wellness care is something you want to add on - Lemonade prices preventative packages from +$10/month and Spot prices its Platinum cat preventative add-on at $24.95/month.

faqs.q: Is Lemonade or Spot cheaper?
faqs.a: On published entry prices, Lemonade is lower for dogs ($10/month against Spot's $15/month) and Spot is lower for cats ($9/month against Lemonade's $10/month). The published averages tell a different story for dogs only: Lemonade says its policyholders pay about $48/month for dogs and about $27/month for cats, while Spot publishes no average of its own. Because Spot's advertised prices carry a $500 or $750 deductible and a $2,500 annual limit for specific pets in specific ZIP codes, the only fair comparison is two quotes for your own pet on the two official sites.

faqs.q: Which one pays claims faster?
faqs.a: Both publish a speed figure, measured differently. Lemonade says it pays 50% of eligible claims instantly through AI and pays approved claims into the bank details you enter in the app. Spot says claims are reimbursed in 48 hours or less, with most processed in under 2 business days, based on its own admin data from 2019 to 2024. Neither figure is an independent measurement, and payment still depends on the claim being covered by the policy.

faqs.q: What are the waiting periods?
faqs.a: Lemonade states 14 days for illnesses and 30 days for orthopedic conditions, with preventative package benefits usable the day after purchase. Spot's sample Accident & Illness policy states a 14-day waiting period for illness including congenital, hereditary and orthopedic illness, starting on the first effective date of coverage, and says a paid Waiting Period Health Assessment can modify it; Spot's preventative care coverage has no waiting period, so those benefits start the next day.

faqs.q: Do they cover pre-existing conditions?
faqs.a: Neither does. Lemonade treats anything your pet showed signs of before the waiting periods are up as pre-existing, while covering accidents and new illnesses as base coverage. Spot excludes pre-existing conditions but reclassifies a cured and curable condition that has been symptom-free and treatment-free for 180 days, except knee and ligament injuries.

faqs.q: Which one has better discounts?
faqs.a: Lemonade publishes a multi-pet discount whose eligibility depends on where you live, a bundle discount with other Lemonade policies, and a discount for paying annually instead of monthly. Spot publishes 10% off every pet enrolled after the first, an advertised 20% employee discount through employer benefits (up to a 10% group discount plus up to a 10% multi-pet discount on 2nd+ pets, varies by state) and Spot Perks with $2,500+ in brand discounts. Neither brand publishes a promo code page in its official sitemap, so a code you find on a third-party site is not something either brand publishes.

faqs.q: Can I use my own vet with either brand?
faqs.a: Yes in both cases. Lemonade says you can go to any vet in the United States as long as they are licensed to provide vet care in their state, and Spot says you can visit any licensed vet in the United States or Canada. Both reimburse you rather than paying the vet directly, so you settle the bill and submit the claim.

faqs.q: Which is better for an older pet?
faqs.a: Spot is the one that publishes an age policy: it covers puppies and kittens from 8 weeks old, states there is no upper age limit and no vet exam to enrol, and also states that premiums are based on your pet's current age and may increase at renewal. Lemonade does not publish a minimum or maximum enrolment age on the pages read here, so its age terms are not published on the official site.

articles.disclaimer: This page is not affiliated with Lemonade or Spot. It repeats only what each brand publishes on its own official pages, with the condition attached to each figure; policy terms always govern and your quote will differ. Facts last checked 2026-09-25.

blocks.h2: How this comparison is built
blocks.html:
There is no neutral score for Lemonade vs Spot. What this page does instead is put the figures each company publishes on its own website side by side, keep the conditions attached to every figure, and link to the page it came from. No figure here is estimated, scored or taken from a third-party comparison site, and where an official page does not publish something, the cell says not published on the official site.

All figures were read from lemonade.com and spotpet.com on 2026-09-25. Spot's waiting-period wording comes from the sample Accident & Illness policy PDF that spotpet.com/sample-policy links to (California form PET-P-20000-CA-IAIC-1024); state forms differ.

The two brands also publish different kinds of numbers: Lemonade publishes averages and state tables, Spot publishes claim turnaround and guarantee windows. A blank cell in the table below usually means the other brand simply publishes that category of figure and this one does not.

blocks.h2: Lemonade vs Spot - official published figures only
Where each one wins on the published facts
blocks.html:
Lemonade, if you want the lower published dog price and instant partial payment. Its cost guide lists policies starting at $10/month, averages of about $48/month for dogs and about $27/month for cats, five deductible options ($100 to $1,000), annual limits from $5,000 to $100,000, the statement that adjusting coverage levels might lower the premium by 10% or 15%, and the claim that 50% of eligible claims are paid instantly through AI. Source: lemonade.com cost guide and lemonade.com/pet-insurance, checked 2026-09-25.

Spot, if published claim speed, age terms and a refund window matter most. It publishes claims reimbursed in 48 hours or less with most processed in under 2 business days (its own admin data 2019-2024), a sample claim of $11,110 back on a $12,345 bill, no upper age limit and no vet exam to enrol, a 30-day money-back guarantee (15 days in ME, LA and WA; not available in NY), a 10% multi-pet discount on every pet after the first, and a preventative add-on whose benefits start the next day. Source: spotpet.com, spotpet.com/sample-policy and spotpet.com/dog-insurance, checked 2026-09-25.

blocks.h2: How to choose without a fake ranking
blocks.html:
Run the brands' own test against each other: take one configuration - a $500 deductible, an 80% reimbursement rate and a $2,500 annual limit - and request the same quote for the same pet at lemonade.com and spotpet.com. Then compare those two quotes with each other, not with the advertised figures above, because advertised figures carry conditions (Spot's dog price assumes a specific 2-year-old dog in ZIP 32009).

Three checks that change the outcome more than the brand name: (1) the waiting period before coverage starts - 14 days for illnesses at Lemonade and 14 days for illness in Spot's sample policy, with different orthopedic wording; (2) whether a condition your pet already has counts as pre-existing - neither brand covers them, but Spot publishes a 180-day symptom- and treatment-free rule for curable conditions that Lemonade does not; (3) whether you want wellness care bundled in - Lemonade prices preventative packages from +$10/month and Spot prices its Platinum cat add-on at $24.95/month with a $450 annual benefit.
